briefs.headline: Atamifuji topples Onosato and shares the Kyushu lead with Wakamotoharu after Day 10
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association's tournament leaders page lists two rikishi (wrestlers) at nine wins and one loss after day 10 of the Kyushu basho (tournament) in Fukuoka on Tuesday, sekiwake Atamifuji and maegashira (rank-and-file) 7 Wakamotoharu, with four at eight wins and two losses: yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato, ozeki (champion) Kirishima, maegashira 7 Kinbozan and maegashira 14 Dewanoryu. Per the SumoDB results table for the day, Atamifuji pushed out Onosato for his second win over a yokozuna in two days after beating Hoshoryu on Monday, handing Onosato a second loss; ozeki Aonishiki threw Kirishima with an underarm throw to knock him off the lead and reach six wins; Wakamotoharu forced out Asahakuryu for an eighth straight win; yokozuna Hoshoryu sidestepped Takerufuji at the charge and won by tsukiotoshi (thrust down) to even his record at five wins and five losses, sending Takerufuji to a make-koshi (losing record) with an eighth loss; ozeki Kotozakura was forced out by maegashira 3 Hakunofuji and is also at five and five; and komusubi Churanoumi, the former Mimoumi, fell to a ninth loss. Kotoeiho returned from six days out with a herniated cervical disc and beat Daieisho. In juryo (the second division) all three leaders lost: Onokatsu beat Wakatakakage to end his nine-bout run, Enho beat Tamashoho and Kagayaki beat Asahifuji, leaving the three level at nine wins and one loss on the JSA table. The final day is Sunday, Nov. 22.

briefs.headline: Chargers beat the Ravens 23-20 in Baltimore for their first win of the season
briefs.summary: Justin Herbert ran 22 yards for a first-quarter touchdown and Omarion Hampton carried 22 times for 105 yards and a score as Los Angeles beat Baltimore 23-20 at M&T Bank Stadium on Monday night before 69,679, per ESPN's box score. The line score was Los Angeles 10, 7, 3, 3 against Baltimore 0, 10, 3, 7: Cameron Dicker kicked field goals of 38, 34 and 35 yards, and Derrick Henry scored on runs of 2 and 1 yards, the second with 10:23 left, for a Ravens offense held to 10 rushing yards on his 10 carries. Jacoby Brissett, starting for Baltimore, was 33 of 49 for 340 yards with an interception by Del'Shawn Phillips; Mark Andrews caught eight passes for 82 yards and Zay Flowers six for 74. Herbert was 12 of 18 for 129 yards and Tre' Harris caught five for 86; Dalvin Tomlinson had two sacks. The Ravens had more yards, 347 to 287, and more first downs, 22 to 15, but gave the ball away twice while the Chargers had no turnovers. The Chargers are 1-8; the Ravens are 4-6 and have dropped five straight.

briefs.headline: Magic outscore the Celtics 40 to 28 in the fourth and win 115 to 105 at Boston
briefs.summary: Orlando trailed by eight after three quarters and outscored Boston 40 to 28 in the fourth to win 115 to 105 at TD Garden on Monday, per ESPN's box score; the quarters went Orlando 20, 30, 25, 40 against Boston 17, 24, 36, 28. Desmond Bane led the Magic with 24 points and eight rebounds and Franz Wagner had nine assists; Jayson Tatum had 24 points and 12 rebounds for Boston, which had set a franchise record with a 42-to-9 first quarter against Dallas on Sunday. Orlando is six wins and seven losses and has won four straight; the Celtics are 11 wins and three losses and dropped behind Philadelphia, 12 wins and three losses, which beat Brooklyn 135 to 123 on 37 points from Joel Embiid and 31 from Jaylen Brown. Elsewhere, Jeremiah Fears had a triple-double of 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists as New Orleans beat Golden State 115 to 94, holding the Warriors to 11 points in the first quarter, and Giannis Antetokounmpo had 20 points, 13 rebounds and six assists as Miami beat Houston 128 to 110 for a fifth straight win.

briefs.headline: Cuylle scores twice as the Rangers beat the Canadiens 3-1
briefs.summary: Will Cuylle scored two goals and New York beat Montreal 3-1 at Madison Square Garden on Monday, per ESPN's box score; the Rangers scored twice in the second period and once in the third, and Phillip Danault, assisted by Lane Hutson, had Montreal's goal in the second. The Rangers are 13-8-1; the Canadiens are 12-5-4. In Salt Lake City, Brock Boeser had a goal and two assists as Vancouver beat Utah 3-2, with both Utah goals coming in the third period; the Canucks are 5-17-1.

waters.reading: 92.1 cfs, 1.59 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow and steady on stage against 106 cfs and 1.67 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the gauge at Dyer as falling, but Monday's paper carried 93.8 cfs and 1.6 feet at the same hour, so the river has given up less than 2 cfs in 24 hours and the 106 cfs the comparison names is Sunday's reading, the 48-hour quirk again: the Saturday bump is spent and the Williams is settling toward its late-autumn base flow. At 92 cfs it is a long-leader, small-fly problem in low, clear water, with the fish on the pocket-water lies and the tailouts rather than the seams, and after another frosty night the midday hours fish best once the sun is on the water. A size 18 to 20 midge or a small Blue-winged Olive nymph under a soft indicator on a long leader through the slower pockets and the tailouts is the pattern, a stonefly nymph as the point fly in the deeper plunge pools where the larger fish hold in cold water, and a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks in the first and last hour of light.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.97 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 25.03 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.0 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool with ordinary bank access, six hundredths of a foot under Monday's printed reading and steady. The wing dams and the riprap are showing rock and the water is clear enough to fish structure rather than the slack behind it: shad are the forage, so a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked down the face of the wing dams and along the riprap is the pattern, slowed down for water that saw frost inland again overnight, with a jig and crawfish on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish holding off the current. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged; this is the pool side.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.0 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.17 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.0 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool and steady, down from the 26.56 feet and rising that Monday's paper carried: the water the dam was passing on Monday has moved through and the lower gauge is back where it sat on Sunday. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid and catfish setup, with less current to work with than Monday; the riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks. Huntington is the downstream bracket, 30-odd river miles below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 1:22 AM at 3.0 ft, low 7:34 AM at 0.8 ft, high 1:48 PM at 3.6 ft, low 8:21 PM at 0.8 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 12:31 AM at 3.4 ft, low 6:18 AM at 1.2 ft, high 12:50 PM at 4.1 ft, low 7:18 PM at 1.0 ft. Water 58.1F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon first quarter, 52% illuminated, 7.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 1:22 AM and 1:48 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All eight events land inside Tuesday on both stations for once, the sound's first high 82 minutes after midnight. The sound lags the surf by 51 minutes on the overnight high, 76 on the morning low, 58 on the midday high and 63 on the evening low, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills; the table is about 45 minutes later than Monday's, the midday flood climbs 2.8 feet from the 7:34 low to the 1:48 high and the evening ebb drops the same 2.8 feet, and at first quarter and 52% the moon is at the neap, so the inlet current is as easy as it gets this month. The water at Beaufort read 58.1F at 5:30 a.m., down 1.3 degrees from Monday's reading after a third cold night; NWS Wilmington's only active product on the coast at 5:45 a.m. was a Frost Advisory for inland New Hanover County until 9 a.m., with nothing for Pender or Onslow and no rip current or beach hazards statement. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 16 days old, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the local piers catching a few big red drum of 32 inches and up on the north end of the island in the wind, a mix of smaller red drum and the occasional speckled trout in the sound with the focus shifting to almost exclusive trout action as the weather cools, and Spanish and bluefish slowed by the wind; Native Son says stable weather should put the area into trout mode, with the deeper seams of 5 to 8 feet in the main creeks the target and cut bait the best bet for scattered reds; Speckled Specialist reports tons of smaller trout with fish to 28 inches mixed in, live shrimp under a cork in 4 to 16 feet of water, 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic if throwing artificials, and black drum to 18 inches over structure on the same float; Carolina Flats says topwater locates trout schools early and the reds are in a last blitz on the oyster and grass banks before the bait thins; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot at night and thick bluefish early, and Surf City Pier pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom. Tied to today's table and a sound now in the upper 50s, the 7:34 low falls in the cold and the window is the top of the flood and the first of the ebb, roughly 12:30 to 3:30 p.m., once the sun has been on the flats: trout in the 5-to-8-foot creek-channel seams and along the ICWW channel edge on a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly, or a live shrimp under a popping cork drifted over the oyster bars at the creek mouths as the water starts to leave the grass. Red drum want the last of the fall, roughly 5:30 to the 8:21 p.m. low, which runs well into dark, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges, or a soft plastic on the oyster and grass banks in the last of the light; the flooded-grass window for a weedless gold spoon is the hour before the 1:48 high. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood; bluefish are the beach fish on a metal jig in the early morning. Flounder are release only.
waters.source: NOAA CO-OPS 8657813 (sound), 8657419 (surf), 8656483 (Beaufort); Fisherman's Post, Topsail/Sneads Ferry November 2026 report (Nov. 1); reference/topsail-fishing.md seasonal calendar; NWS Wilmington; NCDMF
